definition: Pipeline Construction is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Pipeline Construction is
theory.body: Pipeline Construction describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Pipeline Construction is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Pipeline Construction matters
theory.body: Without Pipeline Construction, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Pipeline Construction works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Pipeline Construction follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Pipeline Construction.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Pipeline Construction
theory.body: Pipeline Construction offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
